## WF4 - the needs-attention queue

Every other workflow names this one as its **error workflow**, so a node that throws
anywhere in WF0, WF1 or WF2 arrives here instead of vanishing into an execution list
nobody opens.

**A dead letter is what a park is not.** A park is a run that stopped honestly and left
its work behind, addressable by version id (BUG-017). A dead letter is a run that DIED:
there is no version to attach anything to, and the only thing left is the question *what
needs a human right now*.

So the row has to be actionable **on its own**. It carries the trace_id where one exists,
the workflow and node that failed, the message, and the execution id - because a dead
letter with a stack trace and no trace_id is a log line, and one with a trace_id and no
detail is a notification.

**It must be ACTIVE, and that cost a drill to learn.** n8n 2.x only builds its workflow
dependency index from PUBLISHED workflows, so an inactive error workflow is never invoked -
silently. WF2 failed correctly, the routing was correct, and nothing happened. The drill in
review-ui/scripts/drill-service-unreachable.mjs is what turns that back into a red result if
it ever regresses.

### The retry here is the point

The commonest reason WF4 runs at all is that the review service went away - which is also
the reason WF4's own write would fail. Five tries, three seconds apart, so the queue entry
survives a restart of the very thing it is reporting on.

If every try fails the run still ends: an error handler that throws has nowhere to go.
